attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. He endorses them.

semantics.note: Adding 'via AI startups' is faithful to the paragraph around the quote. 'Held up by' is a claim about dependence, so the causal kind is correct. No horizon or quantifier is lost.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: material dependence, not just having some venture-backed customers. Using Q3 2026 as the window is a reasonable choice for a present-tense claim.

evidence.note: Ramp says 80% of sampled OpenAI/Anthropic spend comes from 1% of firms. That shows concentration in Ramp's sample only. It does not say how those firms are funded or what share of total provider revenue they make up.

reviews.rationale: The packet has nothing linking either provider's revenue to customers' funding sources or to subsidised token buying. Ramp's concentration figure is context only. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition can be checked from this evidence.

attribution.note: Zitron states the 2GW figure as reporting by him and Bloomberg, so it counts as his own claim. The claim about Microsoft's announcements is also his.

semantics.note: 'Only' and 'despite' match the contrast in his 'even though'. Both factual parts are kept: about 2GW of AI capacity, and roughly 1GW added in each of three quarters.

contract.note: The contract scores the two facts separately and does not test the implied conflict. It reads 'last three fiscal quarters' as the last three reported before Oct 13 (Dec, Mar, Jun quarters). Both choices are reasonable, but they decide the result, and the contract flags this.

evidence.note: A Sept 2026 secondary write-up of Bloomberg says about 2GW of Microsoft's 12GW runs on AI-specific chips. This matches the approximate figure.
Microsoft's Dec 2025 quarter: 'nearly one gigawatt of total capacity' added. Company disclosure.
Microsoft's Mar 2026 quarter: 'another gigawatt of capacity' added. Company disclosure.
Microsoft's Jun 2026 quarter: 'another gigawatt of capacity' added. Company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: Both parts of the support condition are met. Reporting of Bloomberg puts AI-chip capacity at about 2GW, and Microsoft's three reported quarters each say about 1GW was added. Microsoft describes those additions as total capacity, so the implied contradiction is not shown. The contract does not score that implication.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. He endorses them.

semantics.note: Both 'vast majority' claims and both 'near-perpetual funding' claims are kept. It is a present-tense factual claim about two layers of revenue.

contract.note: Reading 'vast majority' as an overwhelming share and 'near-perpetual' as repeated outside financing is fair. The H1 2026 window and the choice to combine the two labs are the evaluator's choices, and the contract flags them.

evidence.note: Ramp finds 80% of sampled spend comes from 1% of firms. It does not identify those firms as AI startups, cover all lab revenue, or show how they are financed.
Microsoft reports $24.1B of FY2026 OpenAI-related revenue, including revenue share. It gives no denominator for all hyperscaler AI revenue, and the period does not match.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet gives hyperscaler AI revenue shares by customer, lab revenue shares from startups, or the cash-flow picture showing dependence on funding. Both evidence items are context only. The claim cannot be settled on this evidence.

attribution.note: Zitron's own claim about how the SiliconData index works. He endorses it.

semantics.note: 'Overwhelmingly' is kept, and so is his definition of spot pricing as the price to rent right now. It is a firm factual claim about the methodology.

contract.note: The plain reading (immediate rental prices dominate the index's effective weighting) is fair. Assessing the methodology in force at publication is reasonable.

evidence.note: The Aug 2026 methodology adjusts for on-demand, reserved and spot rentals and weights by provider. It does not disclose the weights by rental type, so it cannot show dominance either way.
The Mar 2026 blog says the index covers reserved contracts as well as spot and normalises prices with a proprietary method. Including reserved prices does not show how much influence they have.

reviews.rationale: The index takes in several rental types, but the effective weights and adjustment coefficients are not disclosed. Neither the support condition (spot dominance) nor the contradiction condition (substantial long-term influence) can be checked with this evidence.
